passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to command the Israelites.
The Israelites must bring pure oil.
The oil must come from pressed olives.
The oil is for the light.
The lamps must burn continually.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ צַ֞ו אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִקְח֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ שֶׁ֣מֶן זַ֥יִת זָ֛ךְ כָּתִ֖ית לַמָּא֑וֹר לְהַעֲלֹ֥ת נֵ֖ר תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Outside the veil of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron is to tend the lamps continually before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
Aaron is a priest of Israel.
The Tent of Meeting is the holy place where God meets with His people.
The veil of the Testimony is a curtain inside the Tent of Meeting.
Outside this veil, Aaron must care for the lamps.
Aaron must do this work before the LORD.
He must tend the lamps from evening until morning.
He must do this continually.
God commands this as a permanent law.
This law will last for all your generations.
passages.original: מִחוּץ֩ לְפָרֹ֨כֶת הָעֵדֻ֜ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֗ד יַעֲרֹךְ֩ אֹת֨וֹ אַהֲרֹ֜ן מֵעֶ֧רֶב עַד־ בֹּ֛קֶר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: He shall tend the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
passages.sermon:
Aaron is the high priest of Israel.
Aaron must care for the lamps.
The lamps stand on the pure gold lampstand.
The lampstand is holy and pure.
Aaron must do this work before the LORD.
Aaron must tend the lamps all the time.
He must never stop this duty.
passages.original: עַ֚ל הַמְּנֹרָ֣ה הַטְּהֹרָ֔ה יַעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־ הַנֵּר֑וֹת לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִֽיד׃פ

passages.text: You are also to take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf, and set them in two rows—six per row—on the table of pure gold before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for worship in the Tent of Meeting.
He commanded the people to use fine flour.
You must take fine flour.
You must bake twelve loaves of bread.
Each loaf must use two-tenths of an ephah of flour.
You must arrange the twelve loaves in two rows.
Each row must have six loaves.
You must place the loaves on the table of pure gold.
You must set the table before the LORD.
passages.original: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ סֹ֔לֶת וְאָפִיתָ֣ אֹתָ֔הּ שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה חַלּ֑וֹת שְׁנֵי֙ עֶשְׂרֹנִ֔ים יִהְיֶ֖ה הַֽחַלָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃ וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֛ם שְׁתַּ֥יִם מַֽעֲרָכ֖וֹת שֵׁ֣שׁ הַֽמַּעֲרָ֑כֶת עַ֛ל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֥ן הַטָּהֹ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And you are to place pure frankincense near each row, so that it may serve as a memorial portion for the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God commanded Moses to arrange the bread on the table of pure gold.
God told Moses to place pure frankincense near each row of bread.
The frankincense is for the bread.
The frankincense serves as a memorial portion.
The frankincense is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
passages.original: וְנָתַתָּ֥ עַל־ הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֖כֶת לְבֹנָ֣ה זַכָּ֑ה וְהָיְתָ֤ה לַלֶּ֙חֶם֙ לְאַזְכָּרָ֔ה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD on behalf of the Israelites as a permanent covenant.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the Israelites.
The Israelites must set out bread before the LORD.
They must do this every Sabbath day.
They do this as a permanent covenant.
This covenant lasts forever.
passages.original: בְּי֨וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֜ת בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת יַֽעַרְכֶ֛נּוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד מֵאֵ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place; for it is to him a most holy part of the offerings made by fire to the LORD—his portion forever.”
passages.sermon:
Aaron is the high priest of Israel.
Aaron has sons who serve as priests.
The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons.
Aaron and his sons must eat the bread.
They must eat it in a holy place.
This bread is a most holy part of the offerings.
The offerings are made by fire to the LORD.
This portion is for Aaron and his sons forever.
passages.original: וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְאַהֲרֹ֣ן וּלְבָנָ֔יו וַאֲכָלֻ֖הוּ בְּמָק֣וֹם קָדֹ֑שׁ כִּ֡י קֹדֶשׁ֩ קָֽדָשִׁ֨ים ה֥וּא ל֛וֹ מֵאִשֵּׁ֥י יְהוָ֖ה חָק־ עוֹלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
passages.sermon:
A man lived among the Israelites.
His mother was an Israelite woman.
His father was an Egyptian man.
This man went out among the Israelites.
He got into a fight in the camp.
He fought with an Israelite man.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ בֶּן־ אִשָּׁ֣ה יִשְׂרְאֵלִ֔ית וְהוּא֙ בֶּן־ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּנָּצוּ֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה בֶּ֚ן הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔ית וְאִ֖ישׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִֽי׃

passages.text: The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse. So they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
passages.sermon:
A man lived among the Israelites.
His mother was an Israelite woman.
His father was an Egyptian man.
This man cursed and blasphemed the Name of God.
The people heard him curse.
They brought him to Moses.
His mother’s name was Shelomith.
Shelomith was the daughter of Dibri.
Dibri belonged to the tribe of Dan.
passages.original: וַ֠יִּקֹּב בֶּן־ הָֽאִשָּׁ֨ה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֤ית אֶת־ הַשֵּׁם֙ וַיְקַלֵּ֔ל וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם אִמּ֛וֹ שְׁלֹמִ֥ית בַּת־ דִּבְרִ֖י לְמַטֵּה־ דָֽן׃

passages.text: They placed him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
passages.sermon: The people placed the man in custody.\r\nThey waited for the LORD to tell them what to do.
passages.original: וַיַּנִּיחֻ֖הוּ בַּמִּשְׁמָ֑ר לִפְרֹ֥שׁ לָהֶ֖ם עַל־ פִּ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Take the blasphemer outside the camp, and have all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then have the whole assembly stone him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD said, "Take the blasphemer outside the camp."
The blasphemer is the man who cursed God's Name.
All who heard the blasphemer must lay their hands on his head.
The whole assembly must stone the blasphemer."
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ הוֹצֵ֣א אֶת־ הַֽמְקַלֵּ֗ל אֶל־ מִחוּץ֙ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְסָמְכ֧וּ כָֽל־ הַשֹּׁמְעִ֛ים אֶת־ יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וְרָגְמ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־ הָעֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: And you are to tell the Israelites, ‘If anyone curses his God, he shall bear the consequences of his sin.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command for the Israelites.
Moses must speak to the Israelites.
Moses must say this to them.
If any person curses his God, he commits a sin.
That person will bear the consequences of his sin.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֥ישׁ אִ֛ישׁ כִּֽי־ יְקַלֵּ֥ל אֱלֹהָ֖יו וְנָשָׂ֥א חֶטְאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must surely be put to death; the whole assembly must surely stone him, whether he is a foreign resident or native; if he blasphemes the Name, he must be put to death.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to Israel.
God said this law to Moses.
If any person blasphemes the name of the LORD, that person must die.
The whole assembly must stone that person.
This law applies to everyone in Israel.
It applies to a foreign resident.
It applies to a native-born person.
If anyone blasphemes the name of the LORD, that person must be put to death.
passages.original: וְנֹקֵ֤ב שֵׁם־ יְהוָה֙ מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֔ת רָג֥וֹם יִרְגְּמוּ־ ב֖וֹ כָּל־ הָעֵדָ֑ה כַּגֵּר֙ כָּֽאֶזְרָ֔ח בְּנָקְבוֹ־ שֵׁ֖ם יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: And if a man takes the life of anyone else, he must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon: This law is for the Israelites.\r\nIf a man kills another person, he must be put to death.
passages.original: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֥י יַכֶּ֖ה כָּל־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם מ֖וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution—life for life.
passages.sermon:
This law comes from God.
God commands justice for all people.
If a person kills an animal, that person must pay for it.
The person must give another life in place of the animal’s life.
This means the person must make full restitution for the animal.
passages.original: וּמַכֵּ֥ה נֶֽפֶשׁ־ בְּהֵמָ֖ה יְשַׁלְּמֶ֑נָּה נֶ֖פֶשׁ תַּ֥חַת נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: If anyone injures his neighbor, whatever he has done must be done to him: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Just as he injured the other person, the same must be inflicted on him.
passages.sermon:
If a man injures his neighbor, the law applies to him.
The man must receive the same injury he gave.
If he breaks a bone, his bone must be broken.
If he puts out an eye, his eye must be put out.
If he knocks out a tooth, his tooth must be knocked out.
The same injury he caused must be done to him.
passages.original: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּֽי־ יִתֵּ֥ן מ֖וּם בַּעֲמִית֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה כֵּ֖ן יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃ שֶׁ֚בֶר תַּ֣חַת שֶׁ֔בֶר עַ֚יִן תַּ֣חַת עַ֔יִן שֵׁ֖ן תַּ֣חַת שֵׁ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֥ן מוּם֙ בָּֽאָדָ֔ם כֵּ֖ן יִנָּ֥תֶן בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death.
passages.sermon:
This law comes from God.
God gave this law to Israel.
Whoever kills an animal must pay for it.
Whoever kills a person must be put to death.
passages.original: וּמַכֵּ֥ה בְהֵמָ֖ה יְשַׁלְּמֶ֑נָּה וּמַכֵּ֥ה אָדָ֖ם יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them a command.
God said, "You must have one law for everyone."
This law is for the foreigner and for the native-born person.
I am the LORD your God.
passages.original: מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֶחָד֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כַּגֵּ֥ר כָּאֶזְרָ֖ח יִהְיֶ֑ה כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Israelites.
The Israelites took the man who had blasphemed outside the camp.
They stoned him with stones.
The Israelites obeyed the LORD’s command to Moses.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר מֹשֶׁה֮ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת־ הַֽמְקַלֵּ֗ל אֶל־ מִחוּץ֙ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיִּרְגְּמ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אָ֑בֶן וּבְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עָשׂ֔וּ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
